alignments.note: Italic *Touching* supplied before a fronted topical nominal that carries no object marker and no preposition; topicalization is not a case-function, so no morpheme licenses the word (rules 16, 33).

Divine title with its supplied *the* (rule 15). The following verbless clause writes no subject of its own, and the ASV supplies the subject pronoun *He* that this written nominal denotes, so both realizations belong to its one discontinuous unit, headed on the first English occurrence (rule 25). The object suffix of מְצָאנֻהוּ already holds the *him* written for it and is not a home for a second pronoun. Two competing readings were available and were set aside: marking *He* added under rule 17, whose ruling reaches a supplied lexical subject noun answering to no morpheme rather than a pronoun a written nominal denotes; and keeping *He* with the predicate adjective's copular frame, which rule 25 forbids in its own terms, since a referential pronoun is neither the construction's copula nor a presentative dummy. Aligned this way to match אֱלוֹהַּ → *God ... him* at JOB.37.22.
*cannot* fuses the negation with a supplied modal and goes whole to the negative (rule 35).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and phrasal particle *out*, discontinuous around the object pronoun (rules 44, 25).

Construct adjective as predicate of a verbless clause, taking the construction-supplied copula and headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 20). The supplied subject *He* is not the predicate's: rule 25 sends a referential pronoun to the morpheme that denotes it, which is שַׁדַּי standing at the head of the verse.
Nomen rectum, its construct relation recast as *in* (rule 19).
Bare nominal with a supplied *in* stating what it contributes to the clause (rule 33).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative.

review_notes: Corrected in chapter reconciliation: the supplied subject *He* was moved out of the שַׂגִּיא unit and into שַׁדַּי's discontinuous unit under rule 25, matching the treatment of אֱלוֹהַּ → *God ... him* at JOB.37.22. The predicate adjective keeps the construction-supplied copula under rule 20.
The competing readings for *He* — added under rule 17, or kept with the predicate's copular frame — are named in that unit's note (rule 8).
The marginal alternative *Or, to justice . . . he doeth no violence* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
